headline: Weak China and residential demand narrow the outlook
summary_short: A. O. Smith posted Q2 2026 net sales of $1,004.3M (-1% y/y) and net earnings of $124.9M (-18% y/y, diluted EPS $0.91), as 5% North America growth was offset by a 19% Rest of World decline on China weakness. It narrowed FY2026 sales and EPS guidance.
summary_long: North America sales rose 5% to $820.5M on the Leonard Valve acquisition, boiler growth and carryover pricing, offset by lower water heater volumes; organic growth was 3%. Rest of World fell 19% to $194.9M as China sales dropped 28% local-currency. Net earnings fell 18% to $124.9M on a $22.6M restructuring/impairment charge; adjusted EPS $1.03 was down 4%. H1 operating cash flow rose 42% to $253.8M, free cash flow rose 67% to $233.3M. Cash $181.3M; long-term debt rose to $598M on a term loan for Leonard Valve. FY2026 sales growth guidance narrowed to 2-3% (from 2-4%) and adjusted EPS to $3.70-$3.85 (from $3.70-$4.00); buyback target raised 50% to $300M.

drivers.explanation: Higher boiler volumes, carryover pricing actions and a $16M contribution from the Leonard Valve acquisition, partially offset by lower residential water heater volumes.
China sales fell 28% in local currency on continued weak consumer demand and a challenging market environment, partly offset by a $6M favorable currency translation impact.

Primarily due to $22.6M of restructuring and impairment expenses tied to footprint optimization and brand rationalization in the North America water treatment business; adjusted earnings fell a smaller 7% y/y.
Higher steel and other input costs largely offset realized pricing gains in North America, while Rest of World profitability declined on lower China volumes.
Narrowed due to continued softness in residential water heater industry volumes; guidance excludes potential impacts from the China business assessment and recent tariff policy changes.
CEO Steve Shafer cited resilience of the business model despite soft North America water heater demand and a significantly weaker China market, with strong boiler growth and cash flow as offsets.
